Last updated 2026-10-22 16:00 PST

Results of the 7 Oct 2026 P2G runs for SRP268462 (THP-1 ECCITE-seq: a CITE-seq study, so each cell has RNA, surface-protein tags and its CRISPR guide), read sequence by sequence. Julia's page for the earlier run (tvuiwg) stays separate. 5 contrasts, each with up to six models (hash all k-mer, hash SPLASH, new screen 1 all k-mer, new screen 1 SPLASH, combined, combined dict), 21 models in all. Every dropdown switches between them. For every selected sequence the page shows where it sits on its gene, whether it matches the genome, which base differs, how other isoforms read it, and what a local BLAST search found for the ones that do not align cleanly.

1 · Runs · all models updated 2026-10-08 16:32 PST

21 models over 5 contrasts, scored on held-out replicate rep3

Dataset: SRP268462 / GEO GSE153056 · CITE-seq (ECCITE-seq) of THP-1 cells, one acute monocytic leukemia cell line, not patient tumour · curated per-cell guide labels and per-cell surface-protein (ADT) counts · 8 SRA runs · 20,729 cells in the metadata · 3 replicates. Counted over: every contrast × method with an output under the S3 prefixes sent for this page. Each contrast keeps only the cells of its classes. The model is trained on replicates rep1 and rep2 and scored on rep3.

Each row is one model. hash is the P2G stage 3 model; new screen 1 ranks targets by presence ratio between the classes; combined fits one lasso on the union of both candidate sets; combined dict averages an all-k-mer model and a SPLASH model. Binary contrasts report held-out AUC; regressions report Spearman ρ (rank agreement of predicted and measured values), Pearson r (straight-line agreement, the measure most RNA→protein papers use) and R² (share of the variance explained compared with predicting the mean); the table under the runs lists all three.

Pearson r is shown beside Spearman ρ because most RNA→protein papers report Pearson. Both come from the engine’s own metric files on the same held-out cells; the hash all k-mer run saved only Spearman ρ and R², so its Pearson (†) was recomputed afterwards from the final model’s saved coefficients on the same test cells; that rebuild reproduces the engine’s own Spearman to 4–6 decimals. R² below 0 means the model predicts worse than the training average.

1b · Published study updated 2026-10-08 16:32 PST

Papalexi et al. 2021 reports no classifier result, so no published value sits beside P2G's

Goal of the study. Papalexi et al. set out "to explore the molecular networks that regulate PD-L1 expression". THP-1 monocytic leukemia cells were stimulated with IFN-γ and given a pooled CRISPR screen against candidate regulators. Each cell was read by ECCITE-seq for RNA, surface protein (including PD-L1) and guide identity, about 20,700 cells over three transduction replicates. The authors also introduced mixscape, which separates cells where the knockout worked from escapers. The question was which knockouts move PD-L1, not how well RNA predicts PD-L1. Main results: the IFN-γ pathway (IFNGR1/2, JAK2, STAT1, IRF1) is needed for PD-L1 induction. The KEAP1/NRF2 axis regulates PD-L1 upregulation, and CUL3, BRD4 and MYC are negative regulators. Some of this regulation is post-transcriptional, with protein changing without matching mRNA change.
studywhat it measuredAUC / accuracy reported
Papalexi et al. 2021, Nature Genetics · PMID 33649593ECCITE-seq CRISPR screen of PD-L1 regulators in THP-1 cells: guide identity, cDNA and surface protein (including PD-L1) per cell; mixscape KO / NP callsnone: the paper reports no AUC, sensitivity or specificity for predicting guide identity or PD-L1 state
Papalexi et al. 2021 · PD-L1 protein level from RNA (regression)whether the authors predicted the PD-L1 antibody-tag (CITE-seq) value from each cell's RNA, or reported how well CD274 mRNA tracks PD-L1 proteinnone: no regression, R², Pearson or Spearman for PD-L1 protein from RNA. They read PD-L1 protein only as the outcome of each knockout: 5 positive and 3 negative regulators; named in the text are the IFN-γ pathway (IFNGR1, IFNGR2, JAK2, STAT1, IRF1 knockouts lower PD-L1) and NRF2/NFE2L2 on the positive side, CUL3, BRD4 and MYC on the negative side, plus KEAP1 (negative) in the validation screen. CITE-seq PD-L1 and flow cytometry are called "highly concordant" with no coefficient. P2G's best regression, Spearman ρ 0.743 (R² 0.55) on held-out rep3 cells (combined, all k-mer), therefore has no published value to compare against.

The authors give no R² or correlation for PD-L1 protein vs RNA, so P2G's R² 0.55 has no published counterpart. The nearest reference points are our own RNA baselines from the study index. A gene-count elastic net reaches ρ 0.778, a little above P2G's 0.743. CD274 mRNA alone reaches only ρ 0.396, so most of the PD-L1 protein signal comes from the IFN-γ-response state rather than from the PD-L1 transcript. That fits the authors' finding of post-transcriptional regulation. Checked against the full text (PMC8011839) on 2026-10-09.

1c · Classes used · all models updated 2026-10-08 16:32 PST

Two kinds of label, neither a cell type: CRISPR guide identity (the KO contrasts) and one protein measurement, PD-L1 (the PD-L1 contrasts); every cell is a THP-1 monocytic cell

Counted over: the cells of each contrast, joined to the exact train and test cell IDs in each run's run_split.rds. A "KO" cell carries a guide against that gene whether or not the knockout worked: the authors' mixscape KO calls are not deposited, so escaping cells stay in the KO class. The PD-L1 contrasts use the PD-L1 antibody tag of each cell: the state contrast compares the top third with the bottom third, and the level contrast predicts the value itself.

3g · Alternative splicing, mismatches and BLAST-only features · selected sequences, 1% rule updated 2026-10-08 16:32 PST

120 alternative-splicing, 904 mismatch (1 or more) and 516 BLAST-only features (5 of them imperfect) among the selected sequences of the 21 models

Counted over: the selected sequences (non-zero weight) of every model, after the 1% rule: a sequence present in fewer than 1% of training cells is left out (98 selected sequences, almost all from hash models; new screen 1 already requires at least 5%). (a) crosses a STAR junction that is not in the reference transcript; compatible transcripts have that exact intron, incompatible ones span it but splice differently or keep it. (a) also counts a soft-clipped sequence that is full length only on alternative isoforms. (b) edit distance of 1 or more from the aligner that placed it, on a full-length placement (split into 1 and 2 or more); soft-clipped and unplaced sequences have no comparable edit distance and are left out of (b). (a) or (b) is counted once per sequence, with the overlap shown, over the selected sequences and over all stage 3 rows. This follows section 3h of the GSE123813 instructions (Julia, 2026-10-08). (c) placed by neither aligner, but hit by local BLAST (GENCODE, genome, IPD-IMGT/HLA) or NCBI core_nt; perfect = 100% coverage and 100% identity. A sequence can be in more than one group. The same features for every study are collected on the running feature ledger.

6c · Immune genes that vary between people · all models updated 2026-10-22 16:00 PST

Immune genes that vary between people: how much of each model’s score is in HLA and Fc-gamma genes?

Why this matters: a model can learn which person a cell came from instead of which condition it is in, and HLA is the most variable region of the human genome. All cells here come from one cell line (THP-1), that is from one person, so weight on these genes cannot come from differences between people. HLA genes are switched on by interferon gamma, the pathway these knockouts disrupt, so here they can be real signal.

3 of 21 models are flagged: HLA and Fc-gamma genes make up 5% or more of their score.

How this was counted (9 rules)
  • Genes: HLA-A, -B, -C, -E, -F, -G, the class II genes (DR, DQ, DP, DM, DO) and the other HLA loci. Antisense genes ending in -AS1 are left out.
  • Fc-gamma genes: FCGR1A, FCGR1B, FCGR2A, FCGR2B, FCGR2C, FCGR3A, FCGR3B and FCER1G.
  • A sequence counts when the aligner placed it in one of these genes. A sequence the aligner could not place counts when the local BLAST matched it full length to one of these mRNAs, or exactly to alleles of one HLA gene (IPD-IMGT/HLA). The found by column says which.
  • Share of the score: the sequence’s weight as a part of the model’s summed weight. The weight is the same as everywhere on this page: the coefficient times f for the hash method, and the coefficient for the other methods. A model is flagged when these genes make up 5% or more of its score.
  • Higher in: the group the sequence’s weight points to.
  • Known dbSNP variants: each base change against GRCh38 called by P2G was looked up in Ensembl VEP. It counts only when a dbSNP record has the same base. ClinVar comes from the same record.
  • COSMIC: P2G’s own match against COSMIC v104, from the run file. An ID that matches the position but not the base is not counted.
  • Training cells that carry it: the share of training cells in each group that contain the sequence, from the run file. Only the hash and new screen 1 lists record it.
  • HLA alleles matched exactly: the local BLAST against IPD-IMGT/HLA (section 5b). It was run only for sequences with 2 or more mismatches, soft-clipping or no placement; not BLASTed means the aligner placed the sequence cleanly.

Built with the shared tool immune_variants.py, run on this page’s own model tables. Section 6b and the bars in section 3 count HLA only by the gene drawn on the genome, so their HLA shares can differ from the ones here.

9 · All instructions updated 2026-10-08 16:32 PST

Every rule this page followed

Source

Built to match the GSE123813 sequence-review page (artifact 6ChpFqMvKXfBMEbrJT1LsV) and the page instructions in rosabiocom/rosa-skills (population-comparison-site, *_PAGE_INSTRUCTIONS.md). The original build scripts are not in the skill, so this page was rebuilt: Julia's page code (renderer, gene_track_annot.js, styles) is reused, and every data file is regenerated by the shared build in website-artifact/sites/study-build (build_rows.py, run_blast.sh, blast_classify.py, expr_stats.py, lit_fetch.py, build_page.py, assemble.py).

Models

One page per study, every contrast on it. Each contrast has up to six models, chosen in every dropdown: hash all k-mer and hash SPLASH (P2G stage 3, stage3_annotated_target.tsv.gz of each dictionary), new screen 1 all k-mer and new screen 1 SPLASH (presence-ratio final-selected tables), combined (Combined_selected_seq: hash + new screen 1 candidates in one lasso) and combined dict (all-k-mer + SPLASH dictionaries, equal-weight). A slot without an output is listed in section 1 with the reason.

Scores

Binary contrasts: held-out AUC (hash: roc_auc of test_evaluation.tsv at feature_level = anchor_target; the anchor-level AUC of summary_row.tsv is shown for reference). Regressions: Spearman ρ between predicted and measured values on held-out cells, and R², the share of the variance explained compared with predicting the mean.

Weight and direction

hash: lasso_coef × f; the other three: the model coefficient. Positive pushes toward the first class of the contrast, negative toward the second. For a regression, positive raises the predicted value and negative lowers it.

Rows

One aligner per sequence (minimap2 when it placed the sequence, otherwise bowtie2); CIGAR, edit distance and cs all from that aligner. A dotted or empty cell is "none". Gene = GENCODE v46 gene overlapping the drawn position, protein-coding before lncRNA before pseudogene, named before ENSG-only. Rows with no target sequence are "no target recorded" and never placed or searched. SPLASH features of the combined-dictionary model take their sequence from the SPLASH new screen 1 table when it has one.

Isoforms

GENCODE v46 comprehensive. The reference row is MANE Select, else Ensembl canonical. An isoform row is kept only when it reads a selected sequence differently (stopping short is not a different reading); identical readings are collapsed; at most 8 rows; every transcript is accounted for in the caption.

Junctions

STAR star_junction matched exactly to the introns of every GENCODE v46 transcript: reference, annotated alternative, or not annotated (new pairing, one new site, no annotated site).

BLAST

Local first: GENCODE v46 transcripts (blastn-short, dust off, E ≤ 1, ≥ 90% identity, up to 500 targets), GRCh38.p13 top level with alternate haplotypes and patches (word size 11, E ≤ 10, ≥ 95% identity) and IPD-IMGT/HLA 3.65.0. Pool = no confident full-length alignment with ≤ 1 mismatch. Rescue bar: ≥ 30 bases at ≥ 97% identity; transcripts first, then the genome (E ≤ 1e-4). A tie across genes is ambiguous; a genome locus is a position, never a gene. Every sequence no local search explains, and every 5b "no closer match" or "clipped bases unexplained" sequence, was then searched remotely in NCBI core_nt (megablast, word size 16, E ≤ 1e-3, up to 25 targets); the card shows the best hit, its organism and the tie count. Other pool sequences were not sent remotely; a sequence still unsearched would be marked "would need a remote search".

Expression

GEO GSM4633614_ECCITE_cDNA_counts.tsv.gz (GEO GSE153056), CP10K per cell. Each model's two groups are its own train + test cells from run_split.rds (a regression is split at the median of the response). Matrix columns are matched to P2G cells by barcode. Ranks are among genes expressed in the two groups together; a GENCODE name missing from the matrix is matched through NCBI synonyms.

Literature

PubMed title/abstract counts for gene + IFN-γ signalling, gene + PD-L1 / checkpoint, and both, for the 15 heaviest named genes of each model (symbol, full name, NCBI synonyms of 4+ characters with a digit or hyphen). Up to three papers per gene with the abstract sentence that names the gene, verbatim. Each linked paper has a one-line conclusion written from its title and abstract only, with a relevance tag (central, finding, gene list only, unrelated match, no abstract).

Gene census

Groups: the contrast's knocked-out genes, CD274 and PDCD1LG2, MSigDB HALLMARK_INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE (M5913) and HALLMARK_INTERFERON_ALPHA_RESPONSE (M5911). The lookup counts every row, selected or not.

Literature: splicing, mismatches and BLAST per gene

Requested 2026-10-08. For each of the 15 heaviest genes in the literature table (3f), two columns summarise that gene's selected sequences (non-zero weight) in the chosen model: alternative splicing (STAR junctions classed against GENCODE v46, plus sequences exonic only in non-reference isoforms and the mRNA-search junction verdict) and mismatches · BLAST (edit-distance strata 0 / 1 / 2+, soft-clipped and unplaced counts, the local BLAST verdicts, and NCBI core_nt hits). A sequence belongs to the gene when it lies in the gene's track, or its stage-3 gene_name, junction annotation or BLAST transcript hit names the gene.

Feature report (section 3g) and the running ledger

Requested 2026-10-08. Every rebuild runs feature_report.py on the selected sequences (non-zero weight) of every model and keeps the ones in three groups: (a) alternative splicing, a STAR junction not in the reference transcript, with the GENCODE v46 transcripts compatible with it (that exact intron) and incompatible (span it, splice differently or keep it); (b) 1 or more mismatches from the aligner that placed the sequence; (c) no aligner placement but a BLAST hit (local, then NCBI core_nt), perfect or imperfect. The 1% rule is applied: a sequence present in fewer than 1% of training cells is left out (hash rows: Train_prev weighted by class size; new screen 1 already requires 5%; combined rows take the share of the same sequence in the hash or new screen 1 table). build_ledger.py then collates every study into the running feature ledger with study, phenotype, label basis, model, gene, direction, target rank, coefficient, weight and share of cells.

Not done

Cell-type marker status is not computed: both classes are THP-1 cells, so it cannot separate them. LitVar2 variant papers were not run. Never downloaded raw reads.

Published study

Papalexi et al. 2021 (PMID 33649593, PMC8011839) reports no AUC, sensitivity or specificity for guide identity or PD-L1 state.
